summary: Two V5 directional claims (forward NonIncreasing with 100 general-integer projection pairs, reverse Equal zero extension) certify a dominance normalization of test24: 7,693 link-only binaries and their rows deleted and 79 disjoint covering rows flipped G to E at rhs 1. It is optimality-preserving, not feasible-set equality, and its exclusion scope exists only as prose.
claims: forward (reverse=false, both integer modes): objective NonIncreasing, projection = 100 pairs [10000,2307]..[10099,2406], the general-integer y coordinates
reverse (reverse=true, both integer modes): objective Equal, projection = [[2307,10000]..[2406,10099]], the zero extension of every deleted coordinate
contract string claims only this much: no bijection, no preservation of every original objective level, no full LP equality claim
the reduction is deliberately not feasible-set equality: original excess coverage and optional selections are dropped, keeping feasibility status, minimum objective and every retained y choice
edit list behind the proof: 7,693 removed binaries each with exactly one removed link row, 79 covering rows G to E at rhs 1, no other semantic change
proof_encoding: forward block: IntervalLift over 2,149 intervals (lower and upper endpoint expression lists plus box premise checks per pair) whose body is one Return{map,checks}
reverse block: one Return{map,checks} whose map sets every deleted coordinate to zero and preserves all retained coordinates
steps are Lin (Le/Eq/Int), EqPair and local Cases/Split in integer mode; refs VarLower/VarUpper/VarInt/RowLower/RowUpper/RowEq/Local/Exact
facts are scoped per branch with ChainMap; SparseBuilder carries model, id counter and fact scope; the RPA is a single JSON document under header RPA 5
certificate carries no bijections and no points (verify statistics bijections=0, points=0), so all of its strength is the two directional claims
agent_manual_work: exact MPS reading by hand: whitespace parser for exploration plus an independent fixed-field parser in output/verify.py; 31,438 eval characters over 12 eval cells

exhaustive incidence scans establishing 10,000 link rows x - y <= 0, 79 pairwise-disjoint covers over 2,307 binaries, 100 blocks of 100, 7,693 use-once columns, exact row signatures and absent containments
1.7 MB audit.json enumerating every removed variable (link row, linked y, objective coefficient, bounds, integrality) and every G-to-E change, with source and target sha256
debugging and manually correcting its own artifact serializer after the audit found 7,693 dangling column records that still referenced deleted rows

hand scope reasoning: reject deleting the 2,307 retained links (a=1/10, x=1, y=1/30 satisfies capacity but violates x-y<=0), reject capacity-based feasibility, reject duplicate-row and component decompositions
